apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: storefront
  namespace: k8s-readiness-port
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: storefront
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: storefront
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 2
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c"]
          args:
            - |
              mkdir -p /www && echo ok > /www/healthz && echo storefront > /www/index.html
              exec httpd -f -p 8080 -h /www
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 80
            periodSeconds: 2
            failureThreshold: 2
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: storefront
  namespace: k8s-readiness-port
spec:
  selector:
    app: storefront
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: http

content.text:
I fixed `web.yaml`: the readiness probe was checking port 80, but the app listens on 8080. The probe now uses the named port `http` (8080). It is still an HTTP check on `/healthz`.

I applied it to the cluster and the rollout finished. The `storefront` Service now lists both pod endpoints, on port 8080. I didn't send a request to `http://storefront/` itself.

The manifest doesn't create the `k8s-readiness-port` namespace, so the verifier has to create it before applying.
